**Price check**
- Google Finance: ₹2,183.00 at 19 Nov, 3:30 pm IST (+1.39%).
- Screener: ₹2,181.00 close on 19 Nov (headline ₹2,180).
- The two agree. Earlier datapoints: blinkx ₹2,263 (11 Nov); MarketScreener ₹2,247 (9 Nov). The 52-week range is ₹1,336–2,979 (high on 10 Aug 2026), so it is now about 27% off the high.
- Recomputed: TTM EPS ₹108.17 (20.75 + 27.50 + 29.46 + 30.46), giving a **P/E of 20.2**. Market cap is about **₹3,730 cr**, debt is about ₹18 cr, and the FY27 EBITDA floor is ₹310 cr, so EV/EBITDA is about 12x.

**Annual figures (₹ cr)**
| FY | Sales | OPM | PAT | ROCE | Borrowings | CFO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY22 | 449 | 28% | 87 | 31% | 12 | 115 |
| FY23 | 501 | 31% | 109 | 36% | 8 | 113 |
| FY24 | 545 | 31% | 119 | 36% | 5 | 118 |
| FY25 | 727 | 29% | 149 | 41% | 4 | 101 |
| FY26 | 768 | 31% | 173 | 39% | 61 | 197 |
| TTM | 836 | 33% | 185 | – | 18 | – |

Over five years, CFO is ₹644 cr against PAT of ₹637 cr, about 1.0x. Debtor days are stable at 59–78.

**Quarterly figures (₹ cr)**
| Quarter | Dec-24 | Mar-25 | Jun-25 | Sep-25 | Dec-25 | Mar-26 | Jun-26 | Sep-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 186 | 182 | 186 | 194 | 182 | 205 | 224 | 224 |
| YoY | +39% | +22% | +3% | +9% | −2% | +13% | +20% | +15% |
| OPM | 32% | 31% | 27% | 31% | 32% | 33% | 34% | 34% (company: 34.34%, a record) |
| PAT | 41 | 47 | 35 | 55 | 36 | 47 | 50 | 52 |

Sep-26 PAT was down 6% YoY only because Sep-25 included ₹12.8 cr of one-off exceptional income. Operating EBITDA was +27% YoY.

**Shareholding**
| Holder | Dec-24 | Sep-26 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promoter (ADI BPO) | 68.34% | 68.34% | Flat |
| FII | 2.02% | 1.49% | Falling (tiny) |
| DII | 0.43% | 2.11% | Rising |

Shareholders rose from 18.3k to 26.3k. This is a very under-owned stock. Pledge was not independently verified; none is flagged in the aggregator data I saw.

**What drives the story**
- The margin reset is sustained: OPM went from 24% (FY20) to 31% (FY23–26) to 34% now, with ROCE in the 36–41% range.
- The named causes:
  - Operating leverage in edtech/content platforms.
  - The **Corporate Learning** segment: EBITDA up 98% YoY in Q2.
  - Subscription revenue from **Unbound Medicine**, an AI/healthcare acquisition that contributed ₹41.6 cr in H1.
  - Billed clients rose about 90% to 933, which reduces concentration.
- Almost all revenue comes from US, UK and EU publishers and learning companies, while costs are in India. It is a pure play on the rupee with no freight exposure.
- The FY27 EBITDA floor was raised from ₹300 cr to at least ₹310 cr.

**Bull case**
- FY27 EBITDA of ₹315 cr gives PAT of about ₹205 cr (EPS about ₹120).
- FY28: management targets ₹1,500 cr revenue, but that **explicitly requires M&A**. Organically, about ₹950 cr revenue at 33% OPM gives EPS of about ₹140.
- At 22x that is about ₹3,080, roughly 1.4x. An accretive acquisition adds to this.

**Stated philosophy and fees (firm's own website)**
- The firm's stated philosophy: "All intelligent investing is value investing. We predominantly follow the principles of classical value investing". Decisions may also use "growth, momentum, or event arbitrage strategies". The firm says it is "market cap agnostic" but "predominantly invest[s] in small/midcap stocks". Portfolios are concentrated, "usually 10-12 stocks" per client — [Equity Intelligence PMS page](https://www.equityintelligence.com/portfolio-management-service)
- Fees: 2% p.a. fixed fee on average NAV, plus a 10% performance fee on returns above 10% p.a. Minimum is ₹50 lakh for the PMS and ₹1 crore for the AIF — [Equity Intelligence](https://www.equityintelligence.com/portfolio-management-service)

- **FY19 -31.87% vs +16.45% | FY20 -51.48% vs -25.02%**
- FY21 152.05% vs 72.54% | FY22 23.57% vs 20.26% | FY23 5.83% vs 0.59% | FY24 45.91% vs 30.08% | FY25 6.01% vs 6.65%
- The site's chart puts the EQ PMS index at about 6,500 and the Nifty at about 3,200 by FY24, both from a base of 100 in 2003. That works out to roughly 22% vs 18% CAGR (computed from the chart, approximate) — [Equity Intelligence](https://www.equityintelligence.com/portfolio-management-service)
- An undated APMI listing shows AUM of about ₹1,432.56 crore — [APMI IA Insight](https://apmiindia.org/apmi/IaInsight.htm?IAID=28). An aggregator lists about ₹781.58 crore and 426 clients — [Finec](https://finec.in/portfolio-management/porinju-veliyath-pms/). The two AUM figures conflict and neither is dated, so they are unverified.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:TITAN:cooler-valuation-beats-nifty-to-jun27`
- **Method:** valuation-temperature · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.48 · resolve by 2027-06-30
- **Evidence:** Yahoo close 20-Nov-2026: Titan ₹4,620.0 (52-wk ₹3,751–5,187); Nifty 50 25,800.6. Screener: P/E 57.7 on TTM EPS ₹79.22 (consolidated) vs FY-end P/E (May price ÷ FY EPS) of ~79×, 83×, 86×, 98×, 77× for FY22–FY26 → ~0.7× its own 5-yr median ('cooler than usual'). But TTM earnings are flattered: Q2 FY27 standalone OPM 15% vs 10–11% history included a ~₹490 cr customs-duty gain in jewellery (normalised Titan Jewellery margin 11.1–11.7% per the 11-Nov-2026 call) and gold MTM swings; Q2 standalone sales growth slowed to +8%; coins/investment buying soft.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Valuation-temperature test with a twist: the stock looks cool on reported TTM earnings, but on normalised margins the multiple is close to its usual level. If the method only works on clean earnings, it should not help here; we lean slightly under base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** A single Nifty-50 large cap beats the index over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if (Titan NSE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 4,620.0) > (Nifty 50 close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits/bonuses; dividends ignored.
- **Resolution source:** NSE / Yahoo Finance closes (TITAN.NS, ^NSEI)
- **Sources used:** https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TITAN.NS; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5ENSEI; https://www.screener.in/company/TITAN/consolidated/; https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/TITAN_11112026143915_SEearningcalltranscriptsQ2.pdf
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified

|---|---|---|
| Manual promises the scorer accepts (coverage) | 20/68 (29%) | 23/68 (34%) |
| **Numbers only, both resolved: exact agreement** | **8/11** | **14/14** |
| Same, using the LLM-structured version of each promise | 5/7 | 11/11 |
| After the chain rule, both resolved: exact / direction | 7/12 / 10/12 | 14/14 / 14/14 |
| LLM path after the chain rule: exact | 9/16 | 12/13 |
| Moved goalposts, manual / auto / both | 9 / 12 / 5 | 6 / 2 / 2 |

**The disagreements are boundary cases, not arithmetic errors:**
- SKIPPER "below 4.5%" finance cost: actual 4.63%. The pilot called it missed; the late rule gives
  partly because the next quarter's TTM figure met it.
- ">25% in FY25 and FY26": the pilot gave partly as a composite of the two years; the scorer
  only checks FY26, so it says missed.
- The FY26 "25% plus" revenue chain: the pilot said missed; the chain rule says moved-goalpost
  because the guidance was relabelled "aspirational" and cut without being acknowledged. Arguably the
  stricter reading is correct, but it is a judgment call. The rule pushes SKIPPER's hybrid MCS from
  −0.18 to −0.34.
- UNIPARTS goalposts missed by inference: the Mexico storyline sits under different metric names and
  categories. LLM `chain_key`s fix this partly. The pilot's "H2 > H1 / Q4 highest" shape promise is
  not auto-scorable.

**Coverage is about 30%, not the ~60% the pilot hoped for.** The gap is promises that are financial
but not on screener: segment revenue (polymer, aftermarket, infra), order inflow and order book,
capex, and company-defined working-capital days. The next step is to parse the quarterly results
PDFs (`nse_fetch.py results`) for segment data and feed them in as `--csv`.
